topic: Figma Components, Variants, and Auto Layout
learningObjectives: Create reusable components for common interface elements.
Use variants to represent different component states.
Apply Auto Layout to create flexible and maintainable interfaces.

activities.title: Component Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the structure of a reusable Figma component.

content.concept: Components package reusable interface elements so designers can maintain consistent styling and behavior across a design.
content.tip: Identify the main component, its properties, and the content that can change.

descriptions: The source definition used to create reusable instances.
A reusable copy of the main component.
A component placed inside another component.
A controlled customization made to an instance.

activities.title: Variant Matcher
activities.instruction: Match component states with their appropriate variants.

content.concept: Variants group related component states such as default, hover, active, disabled, and selected versions.
content.tip: Think of variants as different versions of the same reusable component.

activities.title: Auto Layout Builder
activities.instruction: Build a flexible card using Auto Layout concepts.

content.concept: Auto Layout automatically manages direction, spacing, padding, and sizing as content changes.
content.tip: Combine a container, content, spacing, and padding to create a flexible structure.

activities.title: Responsive Component Lab
activities.instruction: Resize the component and observe how Auto Layout responds.

content.concept: Flexible components adapt their dimensions and spacing when content or container sizes change.
content.tip: Observe which elements resize, wrap, or maintain their spacing as the container changes.

separation.learning: Teach the concept through an interactive experience.
